oi.heading: Operating income
oi.text:
First-quarter 2025 operating income was $468 million (+27%, +34% cc), compared to $368 million in the prior year period.

Operating margin increased 4.0 percentage points as the current year period benefited from gains of $142 million on fair value remeasurements of investments in associated companies, partially offset by increased investment in research and development ("R&D"), $13 million of acquisition and integration related items and a negative 0.7 percentage point impact from currency. Operating margin increased 4.7 percentage points on a constant currency basis.

Adjustments to arrive at core operating income in the current year period were $43 million, mainly due to $172 million of amortization and $13 million of acquisition and integration related items, partially offset by gains of $142 million on fair value remeasurements of investments in associated companies. Adjustments to arrive at core operating income in the prior year period were $169 million, mainly due to $166 million of amortization.

First-quarter 2025 core operating income was $511 million (-5%, 0% cc), compared to $537 million in the prior year period. Core operating margin decreased 1.2 percentage points, primarily due to increased investment in R&D and a negative 0.8 percentage point impact from currency. Core operating margin decreased 0.4 percentage points on a constant currency basis.

da_op.text: Alcon defines earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization ("EBITDA") as net income excluding income taxes, depreciation of property, plant and equipment (including any related impairment charges), depreciation of right-of-use assets, amortization of intangible assets (including any related impairment charges), interest expense and other financial income and expense. Alcon management primarily uses EBITDA together with net (debt)/liquidity to monitor leverage associated with financial debts.

nonint.text: For ease of understanding, Alcon uses a sign convention for its growth rates such that a reduction in operating expenses or losses compared to the prior year is shown as a positive growth.

nonop.text: Alcon calculates constant currency measures by translating the current year's foreign currency values for sales and other income statement items into US dollars, using the average exchange rates from the historical comparative period and comparing them to the values from the historical comparative period in US dollars.

pretax.text: For the nine months ended September 30, 2025, Income before taxes includes core adjustments recognized for Aurion in Share of loss from associated companies. The expenses were incurred upon change in control from Alcon's acquisition of a majority interest in Aurion and include accelerated equity-based compensation expense of $2 million, third party professional services of $2 million for legal and accounting fees and third party bank fees of $1 million.

tax.text: • The core effective tax rate 6 for FY 2026 is expected to be approximately 19% to 20%

net.text: Alcon core results, including core operating income and core net income, exclude all amortization and impairment charges of intangible assets, excluding software, all fair value adjustments to contingent considerations from acquisitions, other than changes due to the time value of money, product discontinuation charges, net gains and losses on fund investments and equity securities valued at fair value through profit and loss ("FVPL"), fair value adjustments of financial assets in the form of options to acquire a company carried at FVPL, fair value remeasurements of investments in associated companies and certain acquisition related items. The following items that exceed a threshold of $10 million, are not operating expenses necessary to the operation of the business and have costs that will vary over periods and are also excluded from core results: integration and divestment related income and expenses, divestment gains and losses, restructuring charges/releases and related items, legal related items, gains/losses on early extinguishment of debt or debt modifications, past service costs for post-employment benefit plans, impairments of property, plant and equipment and software, as well as income and expense items that management deems exceptional and that are or are expected to accumulate within the year to be over a $10 million threshold.

ocf.text: Net cash flows from operating activities amounted to $1.7 billion for the first nine months of 2026, compared to $1.6 billion in the prior year period. Free cash flow was $1.3 billion for the nine months of 2026, compared to $1.2 billion in the prior year period.

da.text: Alcon defines earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization ("EBITDA") as net income excluding income taxes, depreciation of property, plant and equipment (including any related impairment charges), depreciation of right-of-use assets, amortization of intangible assets (including any related impairment charges), interest expense and other financial income and expense. Alcon management primarily uses EBITDA together with net (debt)/liquidity to monitor leverage associated with financial debts.

capex.text: • Capital expenditures are expected to be mid-single digits as a percentage of sales

fcf.heading: Free cash flow
fcf.text: Alcon defines free cash flow as net cash flows from operating activities less cash flow associated with the purchase or sale of property, plant and equipment. Free cash flow is presented as additional information because Alcon management believes it is a useful supplemental indicator of Alcon's ability to operate without reliance on additional borrowing or use of existing cash. Free cash flow is not intended to be a substitute measure for net cash flows from operating activities as determined under IFRS.

net sales.text: Reported net sales for the third quarter of 2026 were $2.7 billion, up 5% on both a reported and constant currency basis versus the third quarter of 2025. Reported net sales for the first nine months of 2026 were $8.2 billion, up 7% versus the first nine months of 2025. Excluding favorable currency impacts of 1%, sales were up 6% on a constant currency basis.

intro.text: Alcon helps people see brilliantly. As the global leader in eye care with a heritage spanning over 75 years, we offer the broadest portfolio of products to enhance sight and improve people’s lives. Our Surgical and Vision Care products touch the lives of people in over 140 countries and territories each year living with conditions like cataracts, glaucoma, retinal diseases and refractive errors. Our more than 25,000 associates are enhancing the quality of life through innovative products, partnerships with Eye Care Professionals and programs that advance access to quality eye care. Learn more at www.alcon.com .

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Lease liabilities
lines.why: IFRS 16 puts every lease on the balance sheet like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Provisions
lines.why: Obligations of uncertain timing or amount (warranties, restructuring, legal claims): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Approximately 6% of our net sales in 2025 were made to customers in China, and we expect that percentage to grow, particularly in our surgical franchise.
No single customer accounted for more than 10% of our global sales in 2025.

The United States accounted for $4.7 billion, or 45%, of total net sales, Japan accounted for $0.6 billion, or 6%, of total net sales, China accounted for $0.6 billion, or 6%, of total net sales, Switzerland accounted for $71 million, or 1%, of total net sales, and the rest of the world accounted for the remaining $4.4 billion of total net sales.
In 2025, the Surgical segment accounted for $5.8 billion, or 56%, of Alcon net sales, and contributed $1.5 billion, or 60%, of Alcon operating income (excluding unallocated income and expenses).
Vision Care segment accounted for $4.6 billion, or 44%, of Alcon net sales, and contributed $981 million, or 40%, of Alcon operating income (excluding unallocated income and expenses).
No customer accounted for 10% or more of Alcon's net sales.
No customer accounted for 10% or more of Alcon's net sales in 2025, 2024 or 2023.

We rely on complex and interdependent information technology systems, including internet-based platforms, to support essential business processes.
Our technology landscape has become more complex as we rely on third-party partners to maintain cyber resilience.

Our migration strategy depends on external vendors and licensing arrangements, which may introduce additional risks if these parties experience outages, fail to meet obligations or encounter security incidents.

We manufacture and source products and materials on a global scale, and our operations and those of our suppliers could be disrupted by a number of factors, including disruptions in logistics; strikes and other labor disputes; loss or impairment of key manufacturing sites; loss of key suppliers; supplier capacity constraints; raw material and product quality or safety

Our success depends on our ability to recruit, develop and retain highly skilled personnel across critical functions, including senior scientific and management teams, researchers, development specialists and manufacturing staff.
Our ability to hire and retain qualified individuals depends on offering competitive compensation and flexibility to reward performance.

Our ability to realize returns on these investments depends on various factors, many of which are outside our control, including market conditions, competitive pressures and the ability of these companies to secure additional financing.
While we currently hold leading positions in several markets, our success depends on maintaining or building on those positions.
Our ability to respond to competitive pressures will depend on reducing costs, maintaining margins, achieving manufacturing efficiencies and sustaining capacity.
Finally, within our surgical business, a considerable portion of sales and growth relies on patient-pay premium technologies in markets where access has been established.
We rely on these groups to recommend our products to their patients and to other members of their organizations.
As a result, the success of these products depends on an ECP’s initial recommendation, which may be influenced by our ability to educate the ECP on our products.
Acceptance of our products depends on our ability to train ECPs and their clinical staff on safe and appropriate use, which takes time.
After training, we rely on ECPs to advocate for our products in the broader marketplace.
We rely on a combination of patents, trademarks, designs and copyrights to protect our intellectual property.
We also rely on trade secrets, know-how and other confidential information to supplement these protections.
We rely on internal controls over financial reporting to ensure the integrity of our disclosures.
In addition, we depend on timely and accurate information from multiple systems and third-party service providers.

As a result, we are exempt from certain provisions applicable to US domestic companies, including rules on proxy solicitation, certain insider reporting and short-swing profit liability obligations and requirements to file quarterly reports on Form 10-Q or current reports on Form 8-K. We are also exempt from Regulation Fair Disclosure and may rely on exceptions from certain NYSE corporate governance requirements.
In each of our markets, we rely on our strong relationships with eye care professionals and consumers to attract and retain customers and expand the market.
Our Custom Paks include both our single-use products as well as third-party items not manufactured by Alcon.
In each of our markets, we rely on our strong relationships with ECPs to attract and retain customers.
